copy constructor: The constructor that builds a new object as a copy of an existing one, `Fraction(const Fraction& other)`; runs for `Fraction b = a;`, `Fraction b(a);`, pass by value and return by value, never for `b = a;` on an existing object. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
reference: An alias for an existing variable, `int& ref = n;`, initialized when declared, never re-seated, used like the variable itself; unlike a pointer it cannot be null and needs no `*`. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
pointer: A variable holding an address, `int* p = &n;`; may be null, may be re-pointed, dereferenced with `*`, members reached with `->`. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
address-of operator|&: Applied to a variable, gives its address; `&success` on a pointer variable gives the address of the pointer itself (`string**`). See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
dereference operator|*: Applied to a pointer, gives the object it points at; `*success` on a `string*` is the string. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
static allocation|automatic allocation: Memory for a variable declared in a scope (`int x = 5; Fraction f(1, 2);`), on the stack, released automatically when the scope ends. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
dynamic allocation: Memory requested at run time with `new` on the heap, reached through a pointer, released only by `delete` or `delete[]`. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
memory leak: Heap memory allocated with `new` and never released with `delete`; prevented by pairing every `new` with a `delete`, freeing in the destructor, or avoiding raw ownership. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
const parameter: `const Fraction& f` promises the function will not modify the argument; with a reference it also avoids the copy and accepts temporaries and const objects. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
const member function: A member function with `const` after its parameter list, `int get() const;`, promising not to change any data member; the only member functions callable on a const object. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
destructor timing: A destructor runs automatically when the object goes out of scope, when `delete` is applied to a pointer to it, for temporaries at the end of their full expression, and for members and bases after the enclosing destructor body, in reverse order of construction. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
uniform initialization|brace initializat: `int x{0};`, the preferred of the three forms (`= 0`, `(0)`, `{0}`) because it prohibits implicit narrowing conversions. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
scope resolution operator|: :: Reaches a name inside a namespace or class (`std::cout`, `Fraction::Fraction`, `Base::f()`, `Date::today()`); the dot reaches a member of an object instance. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
struct vs class: Identical except the default access: struct members are public by default, class members private by default. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
forward declaration: Declaring a name before its full definition (`class Spy;`) so it can be referred to by pointer or reference, reducing header dependencies and breaking circular includes. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
abstract class: A class with at least one pure virtual function (`= 0`); cannot be instantiated. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
interface (C++): A pure abstract class: only pure virtual functions, no data, a virtual destructor; C++ has no interface keyword. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
diamond: Two classes inherit from the same base and a fourth inherits from both; without virtual inheritance the base exists twice and shared members are ambiguous. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
most-derived class: The class at the bottom of a virtual-inheritance diamond; it must call the shared virtual base's constructor in its own initializer list. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
copy-and-swap: `operator=(MyClass other) { mySwap(*this, other); return *this; }`: copy by value, swap every member, let the copy's destructor free the old state; broken by taking the parameter by reference, by `std::swap` on the whole object, or by forgetting a member. See [Part A: the sixteen theory questions](#/comp3522-midterm/theory-questions).
copy elision: The compiler constructing a returned object directly in its destination so one copy disappears; why `A yetAnotherA = foo(littleA);` shows two copies, not three. See [Part B: write the output (Q20, Q27, Q28)](#/comp3522-midterm/output-traces).
std: :stack: A container adaptor over a deque: `push`, `top`, `pop`, `empty`, `size`; last pushed is popped first. See [Part B: the Fraction questions (Q21 to Q26)](#/comp3522-midterm/fraction-program).
ifstream: An input file stream from `<fstream>`; `ifstream in("Fractions.txt"); while (in >> a >> b)` reads whitespace-separated numbers until the file ends. See [Part B: the Fraction questions (Q21 to Q26)](#/comp3522-midterm/fraction-program).
